nodes.label: Correction B - the temporal stack's receptive field is 4, not 20
nodes.rationale: Revision 1's '2 temporal blocks (dilations 1,2)' gives RF = 4, so the encoder would see 4 of the 20 lookback timesteps and ignore the other 16. It would still train, still converge and still produce plausible numbers; the only symptom would be a baffling ablation in which w=20 and w=4 perform identically, and by then Weeks 4-5 would be built on it. Use kernel 2 with dilations (1,2,4,8,16) for RF 32, assert at construction, and pair the assertion with a negative control in which (1,2) must fail. A blocking defect for Day 12.

nodes.label: [CONFIRM-P7] - split the adaptation protocol from the evaluation protocol
nodes.rationale: The most consequential of the confirm items, because it changes what Week 5 can claim. Only the evaluation protocol is frozen, so left-padding short windows for adaptation only is legitimate and needs no bundle change; h=10 and h=15 admit no support target under any windowing choice and are structurally zero-shot; the Week-5 headline is reframed as zero-shot with light short-horizon adaptation. The alternative - re-cutting the Ebola support definition - changes a frozen bundle and invalidates the Phase-2 gate suite. It is also the one Week-3 item that can silently invalidate a whole Week-4 day, since the k-shot sweep and the Day-19 freeze both assume support origins exist.

nodes.label: Scope the spatial claim to timing, not magnitude (§0.9)
nodes.rationale: Per-node standardisation removes cross-node level differences, so the graph layers cannot propagate 'my neighbour has more cases than I do'; what survives is phase and shape co-movement - does my neighbour turn upward when I do. Epidemic wave propagation is a timing phenomenon, so this is real signal, but the manuscript must say which signal it is. This is not a defect to fix: cross-node magnitude is a proxy for population and therefore for geography and therefore for disease identity, so the per-node scaler is a consequence of the disease-agnosticism constraint rather than an oversight. State the trade-off explicitly, because a reviewer who spots it unaided will assume it was accidental.

nodes.label: LTR degree encoding adopted from the EpiGNN lineage
nodes.rationale: Encodes each node's self-loop-inclusive degree as a learned feature using the same D-tilde already computed for the normalisation step, at a cost of roughly 130 parameters, and the weights are shared and disease-agnostic. It is retained despite a caveat that must be stated: degree is a structural quantity correlating with which dataset is being processed, so LTR is the one shared component with a residual disease-identifiability surface - kept because the signal is epidemiologically motivated and the alternative is discarding local transmission structure entirely.

nodes.label: GTR and RAGL checked against the constraints and rejected
nodes.rationale: GTR computes full self-attention over all N nodes, a dense NxN matrix that at dengue's N=7,165 reopens the ~205 MB memory liability already ruled out for A_geo. RAGL's adaptive edge gate uses W_s in R^{NxN}, a learnable parameter matrix sized to one dataset's node count, so it cannot be a shared-weight component of a trunk running across N = 10, 47, 49, 61 and 7,165 - porting it as published would silently break the disease-agnostic-trunk constraint, the same class of silent failure as an unrefit input channel. A constraint-clean version of RAGL's idea (a small N-independent bilinear gate over existing edges) is deferred to Week 6 as an ablation candidate.

nodes.label: sMAPE definition pinned, 0/0 cells excluded
nodes.rationale: Two definitions are in circulation, so pin mean(2|y_hat - y| / (|y| + |y_hat|)) x 100, range 0-200. Cells where both are zero are undefined and must be excluded from the mean rather than counted as zero error: dengue is 78 per cent imputed and Ebola carries four districts that never record a case, so a '0/0 counts as perfect' convention would hand the model a large free credit on exactly the sparsest data.

nodes.label: Ebola metric rules pre-registered before any Ebola number exists
nodes.rationale: A choice made in Week 5 with the data in hand cannot be shown to be independent of it, and a reviewer is entitled to assume the worst. MAE and RMSE are primary; PCC is reported only over districts with at least 5 observed non-zero cells with the qualifying count printed beside it; sMAPE inherits the 0/0-excluded rule and is dropped entirely if qualifying cells fall below 30 per cent of the query set; peak timing excludes districts with no peak and reports the count.

nodes.label: Loss in model space, metrics in count space - asserted
nodes.rationale: Pinball loss is computed in log1p+z space where targets are roughly unit-scale, and all metrics after expm1. Both facts are easy to state and easy to get backwards under the per-origin refit, so guard them with an assertion on target magnitude plus a scaler round-trip test to 1e-5. Mis-ordering the two transforms is the single easiest silent bug in the trainer and it is invisible in the loss curve.

nodes.label: Statistical reporting decided before results exist
nodes.rationale: Five seeds with no intervals will not survive review. All comparisons are paired on identical origin sets; report mean plus 95 per cent bootstrap CI over origins as the primary evidence and a paired Wilcoxon signed-rank across seed-matched runs as supporting evidence. With n=5 the test is underpowered, so lead with the interval and do not claim significance off five points.

nodes.label: [CONFIRM-P8] - learned spatial gate, default on
nodes.rationale: Default chosen so the encoder nests the graph-free model and the spatial channel cannot degrade Week-5 transfer. Paired with a Day-12 gate: forcing g=0 must reproduce the temporal-only model exactly.

nodes.label: [CONFIRM-P9] - annealed edge dropout with the 2x2 reported
nodes.rationale: Default on because one training graph is already known mis-specified and the encoder will be asked in Week 5 to run on a graph built by a different process for a disease with a different transmission kernel. Annealing is required so the gate learns on a trustworthy graph first, and the 2x2 is required because two one-way ablations cannot separate 'augmentation helps' from 'augmentation suppressed the gate'.

nodes.label: Every Day-12 assertion ships with a negative control
nodes.rationale: A gate that cannot fail proves nothing - the Phase-2 discipline carried forward. Each assertion is paired with a planted defect that requires the assertion to fire: no NaN in A-hat, the trunk rejecting C with a TypeError, LTR reusing the degree vector, RF >= 20, g=0 reproducing the temporal-only model, and no shared-trunk parameter with a dimension in {10, 47, 49, 61, 7165}.

nodes.label: Day-11 close-out readings that gate Day 12
nodes.rationale: Both are readings of Day 11's own output rather than new work: the Ebola support-origin count from the per-phase printout, which is the go/no-go on the Week-4 design, and the node-level-mean variance of X[:,:,0] per dataset, without which Task 12.6's ablation cannot be interpreted. Origin counts before phase filtering must match the guide exactly (dengue 1,375, us-regions 751, us-states 326, japan 314); that agreement is the check that the windowing contract was implemented as written.

nodes.label: Ebola enters no loop that chooses anything in Week 3
nodes.rationale: The control that makes a second run visible is not built until Day 20, so the Week-3 rule is behavioural and absolute. Everything needed to size the design against Ebola is already in the guide - 61 nodes, 52 weeks, 27 support cells, 9 of 61 districts carrying support - so there is no reason to open the file.
